what_its_for: Levomilnacipran is used to treat major depressive disorder (MDD) in adults. It helps improve your mood, energy level, sleep, appetite, and overall interest in daily life. It belongs to a group of medicines called serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (SNRIs), which work by balancing certain natural chemicals in the brain.
how_to_take: Take levomilnacipran once daily, with or without food. Swallow the capsule whole — do not crush, chew, or open it. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember. Do not suddenly stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first, as stopping too quickly can cause withdrawal symptoms like dizziness, nausea, or irritability.
dosing: Your doctor will usually start you on a low dose of 20 mg once daily for 2 days, then increase it to 40 mg once daily. Your doctor may gradually increase your dose up to a maximum of 120 mg once daily, depending on how well you respond and how you tolerate the medicine. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your dose.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — unless it is almost time for your next scheduled dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at once to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store levomilnacipran at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of it.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medicine, as it can increase side effects like dizziness and drowsiness. Do not take monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOIs) — such as phenelzine, tranylcypromine, or linezolid — within 14 days of taking levomilnacipran, as this combination can cause a serious and life-threatening reaction. Use caution when driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid taking other medicines, supplements, or herbal products (like St. John's Wort) without checking with your doctor or pharmacist first, as they may interact with levomilnacipran.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the nearest emergency room if you experience: thoughts of suicide or self-harm, unusual changes in behavior or mood, fast or irregular heartbeat, severe headache, sudden vision changes or eye pain, difficulty urinating, unusual bleeding or bruising, severe allergic reactions (rash, swelling of the face or throat, trouble breathing), high fever with confusion and muscle stiffness (signs of serotonin syndrome), or significant increase in blood pressure. Also contact your doctor if you have bothersome side effects like nausea, constipation, sweating, or sexual problems that do not go away.
when_it_works: You may start to notice some improvement in your sleep, appetite, or energy levels within the first 1 to 2 weeks of treatment. However, it may take 4 to 6 weeks or longer to feel the full benefit for your mood and depression symptoms. It is important to keep taking your medicine every day, even if you do not feel better right away. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and over): Use with caution, as older adults may be more sensitive to side effects like dizziness and falls. Kidney problems: Your doctor may prescribe a lower dose if you have kidney disease. Liver problems: No dose adjustment is usually needed for mild to moderate liver disease, but talk to your doctor. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. This medicine may affect the unborn baby or pass into breast milk. Your doctor will help you weigh the risks and benefits. Children: Levomilnacipran is not approved for use in children under 18 years of age.
